_help: Describes YOUR data space to the agents. Copy this file to config/data_profile.json and edit every value. The agent prompts (agents/prompts/*.md) read it at deploy time, so no prompt needs editing. Keep it factual: the agents treat it as ground truth and will not ask the user for it.
coverage: from <first date of data> to <last date of data>
zones: <comma-separated geography names the business uses, for example zone names>
channels: <the sales channels, for example Stores (offline), Online (website and marketplace) or Quick Commerce>
categories: <a handful of example product categories, classes or brands, for example Laptops, Air Conditioners, Mobile Accessories>
standing_scope: <The filters every question must carry unless the user asks otherwise, in one sentence, for example: Merchandise articles only, with Miscellaneous and Charges excluded.>
facts: <One fact per line. State what the data space can and cannot do, so the planner does not plan around data that does not exist.>
Transactions cover <coverage>. Year-on-year views are possible for any period whose last-year dates are inside that range.
Channels are <channels>. Channels must be mutually exclusive when summed. <Say what is always excluded, for example Miscellaneous and Charges.>

Targets: <which plan or target types exist (AOP, SOP, mission targets), at what grain (channel, category, zone, day), and which are comparable with which actuals. For example: zone targets cover Stores only, so compare them with Stores actuals, never with enterprise actuals.>
<Which measures exist only for part of the business, for example margin and markdown for Stores only.>

<How each ratio is defined: which rows and which table give its numerator and its denominator, so an analysis never divides figures taken on different bases. For example: margin % is merchandise profit divided by net sales, both from the cost table on rows where the cost is available, not profit divided by total sales.>
A week is <Monday to Sunday>. A weekday-aligned year-on-year week starts <364 days earlier>.
